argument_summary: Certification is supportable only as a caveated, disclosure-based compliance position. The admissible record shows the current release clears aggregate launch readiness by 2.5 percentage points and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, while also showing a current subgroup regression in the developer-support migration slice. Under the policy text, that combination can still support certification if the current weakness is treated as a material limitation that must be explicitly disclosed, rather than implied to be resolved or excused by prior approval or informal monitoring.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy does not require every current weakness to be resolved before certification; it requires current evaluation results to be reflected in release documentation and material segment weaknesses to be disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. The admissible evidence supports the narrower reading that certification remains compliant if the packet is framed around current aggregate readiness plus explicit disclosure of the developer-support migration limitation. The same admissible policy text also means prior approval and informal monitoring cannot be presented as substitutes for current disclosure or approved mitigation.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is offered as a basis for the decision. The supportable case is policy-based and evidence-based, not urgency-based.
concessions: The developer-support migration slice is a current regression and should not be characterized as resolved.
The record does not include reviewed mitigation, owner risk acceptance, or attached disclosure language.
Prior approval of the same model family is contextual only and does not by itself satisfy the current-release policy requirement.
